qns_content.text: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Which one is not a Mendalian disorder-<\/div>\n"

learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Which one is not a Mendalian disorder-<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text:
"Concept :
Solution: 

Mendelian disorders are caused by mutations in single genes and follow Mendel's laws of inheritance (dominant, recessive, or sex-linked).

Examples:

  • PKU – Autosomal recessive disorder due to mutation affecting phenylalanine metabolism.
  • Royal disease (Hemophilia) – X-linked recessive disorder affecting blood clotting.
  • Pseudo rickets (Vitamin D-resistant rickets) – Often X-linked dominant Mendelian disorder.

 Down's syndrome is not a Mendelian disorder:

  • It is a chromosomal disorder, caused by trisomy of chromosome 21 (i.e., presence of an extra copy of chromosome 21).
It does not follow Mendelian inheritance.
Final Answer : (3)"

options.text: It is sex linked recessive disorder
It is due to mutation in certain genes present on X-chromosome
It occurs in about 8% in female and about 0.4 % in males

learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Which of the following statement is incorrect regarding colorblindness ?<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text:
"
Concept :
Solution: 

 (1) True –

Colour blindness is a sex-linked recessive disorder, inherited via the X chromosome.

 (2) True –

It is caused by mutations in genes that code for color-detecting proteins, located on the X chromosome.

❌ (3) Incorrect –

This statement reverses the actual frequency:

  • About 8% of males are affected by colour blindness.
  • Only about 0.4% of females are affected, because females would need two copies of the defective gene (one on each X chromosome), which is rare.

Thus, the figures are incorrect, and the statement is false.

 (4) True –

For a daughter to be colour blind, she must inherit:

  • One defective X from her carrier mother, and
  • One defective X from her colourblind father.
So, the statement is correct
Final Answer : (3)
"

"

text_solutions.text:
"Concept :
Solution: 

(A) Honey bee → (ii) Haploid-diploid method of sex determination

  • In honeybees:
    • Males (drones) are haploid (develop from unfertilized eggs).
    • Females (workers and queen) are diploid (develop from fertilized eggs).
  • This is called haplodiploidy.
 

 (B) Cockroach → (iv) XO method of sex determination

  • Male cockroach: XO
  • Female cockroach: XX
  • The absence of a second sex chromosome in males determines the sex → XO system
 

 (C) Birds → (i) Female heterogamy

  • In birds:
    • Males: ZZ (homogametic)
    • Females: ZW (heterogametic)
  • So, females determine the sex → female heterogamy
 (D) Henking → (iii) X-body
  • Henking discovered a strange body in some male insects, which he called the X-body.
This led to the discovery of the X chromosome.
Final Answer : (1)"

text_solutions.text:
"Concept :
Solution : 
1. Holandric Gene: This term specifically refers to genes that are located on the Y chromosome and are transmitted exclusively from father to son. Since only males possess the Y chromosome, these genes do not get passed on to daughters.
2. Supplementary Gene: This term generally refers to genes that work together to produce a certain phenotype but are not specifically tied to the Y chromosome.
3. Complementary Gene: Similar to supplementary genes, complementary genes interact to express a particular trait, but again, they are not defined by their location on the Y chromosome.
4. Duplicate Gene: This term refers to genes that are copies of each other and can provide redundancy in gene function. It is not related to the Y chromosome inheritance.
Summary:Holandric genes are the correct term for genes located on the Y chromosome that are transmitted from father to son.
Correct Answer : (4)"
